low.text: Name one owner for whether a bet is worth building.
low.firstStep: Put a single name on the next bet before a ticket is opened.
low.outcome: It is obvious who can stop the work.

low.text: Run a 30-minute customer check before build spend.
low.firstStep: Talk to five users before the next build ticket is opened.
low.outcome: The bet has a customer signal before engineering time is spent.

low.text: Write the bet in one sentence with a stop rule.
low.firstStep: Add one sentence and a stop rule to the top of the spec.
low.outcome: The team can tell when to quit.

mid.text: Move the customer check in front of the spec.
mid.firstStep: Do the customer check before design, not after it.
mid.outcome: Specs start from a customer signal.

mid.text: Score the bet on retention, revenue, or cost before kickoff.
mid.firstStep: Add one of those three numbers to the kickoff note.
mid.outcome: The bet is judged on an outcome, not on activity.

mid.text: Limit new bets to what the team can finish this month.
mid.firstStep: Cap new starts at the number the team finished last month.

high.text: Review the customer result when the feature goes live.
high.firstStep: Book a 20-minute review two weeks after release.
high.outcome: The decision is checked against what customers did.

high.firstStep: Share one stopped bet in the next planning note.

high.text: Pair the decision owner with one engineer before the spec grows.
high.firstStep: Spend 30 minutes together before the spec is written up.
high.outcome: The bet is shaped before it becomes a queue of tickets.

low.text: Put one approved AI coding tool in front of every engineer.
low.firstStep: Pick one tool and turn it on for the whole team this month.
low.outcome: AI coding is available on real work, not only in trials.

low.text: Share a short prompt pack for the repo's real tasks.
low.firstStep: Write five prompts from last month's pull requests.
low.outcome: People start from a known prompt instead of a blank box.

low.text: Check weekly that the tool is used on production code.
low.firstStep: Ask each squad for one production change that used the tool.

mid.text: Give each senior a WIP limit of three agent streams.
mid.firstStep: Set the limit on the board this week.
mid.outcome: Parallel AI work does not outrun review.

mid.text: Require a one-page spec before a second stream starts.
mid.firstStep: Block a second stream until the one-pager exists.
mid.outcome: Agents work from a spec, not a vague ticket.

mid.text: Review AI-written code with the same bar as other code.
mid.firstStep: Add 'who reviewed the AI edits' to the pull request template.
mid.outcome: AI edits are not merged unseen.

high.text: Keep the WIP limit as coding gets faster.
high.firstStep: Leave the limit of three in place for the quarter.
high.outcome: Speed does not become a pile of open work.

high.text: List the files where unreviewed AI edits are not allowed.
high.firstStep: Name auth, billing, and migrations as review-required.

high.text: Measure cycle time of AI-assisted changes on their own.
high.firstStep: Tag AI-assisted pull requests and read the median time on Friday.
high.outcome: You can see whether AI coding is actually faster.

low.text: Automate regression on the top 3 journeys.
low.firstStep: Name the three journeys and record a passing automated test for each.
low.outcome: Those journeys fail the build instead of failing in front of customers.

low.text: Block release if those three tests are red.
low.firstStep: Make the three tests a required check on the release branch.
low.outcome: A red journey cannot ship by accident.

low.text: After every serious incident, add one test before the ticket closes.
low.firstStep: Add that rule to the incident template this week.
low.outcome: The same failure does not return unseen.

mid.text: Move security checks into the merge path.
mid.firstStep: Run the security checklist on every change, not only near release.
mid.outcome: Compliance is not a surprise at the end.

mid.text: Delete manual scripts that duplicate an automated test.
mid.firstStep: Pick the five scripts QA repeats and retire the ones a test already covers.
mid.outcome: QA time goes to gaps, not to repeated clicks.

mid.text: Give QA a queue of failing tests, not a pile of tickets.
mid.firstStep: Route red tests to QA before new manual passes.
mid.outcome: Failures are fixed before the next round of clicking.

high.text: Keep the journey tests running on every change.
high.firstStep: Leave the three journey tests required on each pull request.

high.text: Add a test for the last incident that had none.
high.firstStep: Write that test before the next planning meeting.

high.text: Count how often a red test stops a release.
high.firstStep: Note each stop in the release log for a month.
high.outcome: The tests are earning their place.

low.firstStep: Pick one product area and release it every week behind a flag.
low.outcome: A small change reaches customers the same week it is finished.

low.text: Open a same-day path for low-risk changes.
low.firstStep: Define the risk bar: tests green, no schema change, no personal data.
low.outcome: Small safe changes do not wait for the train.

low.text: Cut the sign-off that waits on people who are not blocking.
low.firstStep: List who must say yes, and remove the rest from the meeting.
low.outcome: Release waits on a decision, not on a calendar.

mid.text: Shorten the train from monthly to every two weeks.
mid.firstStep: Put the next train on the calendar 14 days out and keep it.
mid.outcome: Finished code waits days, not a month.

mid.text: Flag any change that sits more than five days after merge.
mid.firstStep: Add a board column for merged and not released.

mid.text: Make compliance a checklist in the spec, not a gate at the end.
mid.firstStep: Add the checklist to the spec template and block merge until it is ticked.
mid.outcome: Release day is not the first time compliance is asked.

high.text: Review flags that are still off after two weeks.
high.firstStep: Read the open flags every other Friday and delete or ship them.
high.outcome: Flags do not become a second backlog.

high.text: Publish time from merge to customer each Friday.
high.firstStep: Post the median hours in the engineering channel.
high.outcome: The team can see the path getting shorter or stuck.

high.text: Remove one manual approval that has not caught a defect this quarter.
high.firstStep: Pick the approval with no catches and drop it for low-risk changes.
high.outcome: A step that only adds wait is gone.

low.text: Attach one adoption metric to each feature.
low.firstStep: Add one usage event before the feature is called done.
low.outcome: Each new feature has a number you can read two weeks after release.

low.text: Read that number two weeks after release.
low.firstStep: Put a 15-minute read-out on the calendar for the last feature.
low.outcome: The number is used, not only collected.

low.text: Stop judging the quarter on tickets closed.
low.firstStep: Replace the headline number in the review with one customer outcome.
low.outcome: The review talks about customers, not throughput.

mid.text: Tie each bet to revenue, retention, or cost.
mid.firstStep: Pick one of the three for the current bet and write it on the spec.
mid.outcome: The bet has a business number.

mid.text: Drop velocity as the number that decides success.
mid.firstStep: Take velocity off the first slide of the review.
mid.outcome: A faster build is not mistaken for a better outcome.

mid.text: Write down what 'used it' means before build.
mid.firstStep: Add one sentence to the spec: the event that counts as use.
mid.outcome: The metric is agreed before the code exists.

high.text: Review the adoption number when you plan the next bet.
high.firstStep: Start planning by reading the last feature's number.
high.outcome: The next bet learns from the last one.

high.text: Stop a follow-up that shows no movement after two releases.
high.firstStep: Name one follow-up you will stop if the number is flat.
high.outcome: Flat work does not continue by habit.

high.text: Share the number with the people who wrote the code.
high.firstStep: Post the number in the squad channel the day you read it.
high.outcome: The builders see whether customers used the work.
